subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 22, 2026
body:
The geocode-glib conflict that was blocking AcreetionOS-Xlibre builds has been finally resolved, unlocking a fresh ISO release for users craving a clean Arch‑based experience.  

geocode-glib conflict resolved in acreetionos + acreetionos-xlibre  

Development  
Natalie and Darren’s merge of the ‘main’ branch into release‑1 finally squashed the geocode‑glib update clash, so the Xlibre edition can now be rebuilt without hitches. The fix appears in the latest changelog (https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html) alongside a CI tweak that passes -R to gh release create, cutting checkout time in the release job. If you’re curious about the nitty‑gritty, the docs (https://acreetionos.org/docs.html) detail the geocode‑glib package integration and the new release workflow.  

Community  
Igalia celebrated “Twenty‑Five Years Upstream” this week, highlighting two and a half decades of open‑source advocacy. Meanwhile Greg Kroah‑Hartman pushed out three new stable kernels – 7.2.7, 6.18.53 and 5.15.180 – giving everyone a fresh security baseline. AlmaLinux and Debian also rolled out Monday’s security updates, covering kernel, perl‑Net‑DNS, sudo, tomcat, chromium, gimp and more, so staying patched is easier than ever. The project’s Discord (https://discord.acreetionos.org) is buzzing with thanks to the core team for keeping the pipelines smooth.  

Tip of the day  
With the Xlibre build now conflict‑free, try the new ISO using AcreetionMediaWriter from the download page (https://acreetionos.org/flash.html) for a zero‑telemetry install that respects repository sovereignty. After flashing, run ‘pacman -Syu’ to snap up the latest kernel and security patches in one go. Happy hacking!
